facts.text: The male golden whistler shows a bright yellow underside and nape, olive-green back and wings, a black head and chest-band, and a white throat.
facts.quote: The male has a bright yellow underside and nape, olive-green back and wings, a black head and chest-band, and a white throat.

facts.text: Female golden whistlers in Australia are overall dull brownish-grey, though some have yellowish undertail coverts.
facts.quote: In Australia females are overall dull brownish-grey, though some have yellowish undertail coverts.

facts.text: Both sexes of the golden whistler have a black bill, dark legs and red-brown eyes.
facts.quote: Both sexes have a black bill, dark legs and red-brown eyes.

facts.text: The golden whistler has a strong, musical voice.
facts.quote: Australian golden whistlers have a strong, musical voice.

facts.text: Golden whistlers breed between September and January, raising only one brood per season.
facts.quote: This species breeds between September and January.

facts.text: Both parents build the nest, a shallow bowl of twigs, grass and bark bound together with spider web, and share incubation and care of the young.
facts.quote: Male and female both work on the nest, which is a shallow bowl made of twigs, grass, and bark, and bound together with spider web. Only one brood is raised per season and both birds share incubation and care of young.

facts.text: Golden whistler eggs hatch 15 days after laying, and the young leave the nest after just 12 days.
facts.quote: Eggs hatch 15 days after they are laid and the young leave the nest after 12 days.

facts.text: Golden whistlers eat berries, insects, spiders and other small arthropods, usually feeding alone at the lower to middle tree level.
facts.quote: It eats berries, insects, spiders, and other small arthropods. They usually feed alone and obtain food from the lower to middle tree level, or they may alternatively take part in mixed-species feeding flocks.

facts.text: Golden whistlers live in almost any wooded habitat, especially dense forests, and some south-eastern birds migrate north for winter.
facts.quote: The Australian golden whistler can be found in almost any wooded habitat, especially dense forests.

facts.text: The golden whistler was once known as the white-throated thickhead.
facts.quote: This bird was formerly known as white-throated thickhead.
